Alex — thanks, great context.

Quick notes up front: EU ended DST on Oct 25 (CEST->CET). US switches Nov 1 this year, so a meeting on Nov 2 can look like it moves for US participants by 1 hour vs what you think. To avoid surprises I recommend booking based on UTC and listing all three local times with explicit offsets for the meeting date.

Proposed "sweet spot" windows (60 min) that give decent overlaps without an overnight:
- Option A: 13:00 UTC (US West: 06:00 PDT on Nov 2 — early for US execs, not ideal)
- Option B: 14:00 UTC (US West: 07:00 PDT on Nov 2; EU CET: 15:00 CET; APAC SGT: 22:00 SGT) — this is the one I think minimizes pain (CTO would be late evening, EU mid-afternoon).
- Option C: 15:00 UTC — pushes APAC very late (23:00 SGT) so not preferred.

Because of the DST flip on Nov 1 for US we should explicitly confirm what calendar clients will show. If you prefer to avoid across-the-switch days entirely, Nov 4–5 (after US flip) is cleaner.

I created a mutual action plan stub and a short executive agenda and attached them here: [Attachment: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (xlsx)], [Attachment: Nimbus_exec_MOP_v1.pdf (PDF)].

If you confirm B (14:00 UTC), we can:
- Send a calendar invite in UTC with localized labels for each participant
- Bring the CTO portion for the first 20 min, then a technical deep dive with Karthik and Aditya for the remainder
- Record the session and share a short 20-min condensed clip for APAC follow-up

Thoughts?

—Tessa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

We can structure the 60-min as: 20 min exec + 35 min technical walkthrough + 5 min Q&A. For the technical piece we'll highlight latency/cost tradeoffs on typical Nimbus query profiles and show a short end-to-end trace.

- Karthik (SE) brings perf graphs and the trace

—Karthik

Thanks — B (14:00 UTC) looks close to ideal, but one ask: our CTO (SGT) prefers not to do anything later than 22:00 local on a weekday. On Nov 2 14:00 UTC equals 22:00 SGT (good), but because the US flips Nov 1 some of our US partners will see a different time. Given the risk, can we either:
1) Move to Nov 4 at 08:00 UTC (which is 16:00 CET / 16:00 CET for EU and 16:00 CET -> 00:00 SGT so actually worse for APAC), or
2) Keep Nov 2 14:00 UTC but call out in the invite "UTC baseline — double-check your local zone after Nov 1" and share the recorded condensed clip immediately after.

We want to avoid re-scheduling the exec call last-minute, so option 2 plus a recorded APAC follow-up clip is acceptable. Can you confirm you'll include explicit offsets in the invite and a note about the Nov 1 DST flip? Also can we lock down an internal escalation list in case a senior exec can't join and the demo needs to proceed?

Alex
